# dsh-scope
**English** · 简体中文
**Usage statistics for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)** — a lifetime dashboard of your token usage across
every session, plus a context lens for the session you are in.
DeepSeek Harness computes rich token accounting and then shows you none of it. `dsh-scope` surfaces
computes rich token accounting and then shows you none of it. `dsh-scope` surfaces it in two places.

> One of several `dsh` plugins developed under
> `dsh-plugins/` — each an independent
> repo with it
s own release cadence.
## Features
### Usage statistics (sidebar footer)
Open from the sidebar foot — a label when the sidebar is wide, an icon on the rail.
- **Lifetime summary** — cumulative and peak-day tokens, longest session, current and longest streak

s.
- **Token activity** — a 52-week heatmap in three modes: **daily** (each day colored on its own u
sage), **weekly** (each column summed) and **cumulative** (a running total across columns). One grid

reads either as a year at a glance or as growth over time.
- **Time range** — last 7 or 30 days, dr

iving both charts below.
- **Daily token trend** — one line per model, with a wrapping legend and pe

r-day tooltip. Only models used inside the window appear as series.
- **Model usage** — a donut with
the window total in the center and a percentage list beside it.
The whole panel is one request to the plugin's own loopback-only endpoint.
### Context Lens (session header)
Window occupancy for the current session: a live occupancy ring in the header that opens into a segm
ented system / tools / messages composition bar, per-bucket session totals, and KV-cache hit rate. I
t reads the official `token-meter` session projections through `useProjection` — no RPC, no custom w
fficial `token-meter` session projections through `useProjection` — no RPC, no custom wire protocol.
## Requirements

- `dsh` ≥ `0.1.0-rc.6` on your `PATH` (verified against `0.1.0-rc.6` and `0.2.0-rc.2`)
- Node.js 22.
18+ or 24.11+ (for building from source only)

## How it works
**Host half** (`lib/index.js`) — one read-only, loopback-fenced endpoint, `GET /api/dsh-scope/days`.
Aggregation is incremental. Per-session fold state is cached in memory and persisted to `~/.dsh/stor
ages/dsh-scope-cache.json`, and each request folds only the events added since the last fold. Live s
essions fold their in-memory tail; persisted sessions skip work entirely while the backend's opaque
revision is unchanged, and otherwise read only the new suffix, with contiguity checks and a full ref
old when a log was truncated or rewritten. Steady-state cost stays O(new events) no matter how large
was truncated or rewritten. Steady-state cost stays O(new events) no matter how large the logs grow.
Fold semantics mirror `dsh-token-meter`'s `tokenUsage` projection. A usage sample rides an `assistan
t/chunk` (`data.chunk.type === "usage"`) or an `assistant/message` (`data.usage`). A repeated sample
for the same (turn, step) **replaces** the earlier value rather than double counting, re-attributed
to the later event's day and model. Model attribution follows `assistant/message`'s `data.message.s
ource`, falling back to the last `request/header` config.
Beyond token buckets, the fold counts `turn/start` and `tool/call` events per day (feeding the weekl
y and cumulative heatmap tooltips) and tracks each session's first and last event timestamps so the
summary can report the longest session. The payload carries **every** model per day rather than a tr
uncated top-N, so the trend chart and donut always cover all of them.
**Client half** (`lib/client.js`, loaded via the package's `dsh.client` declaration):
- `sidebar.footer.action` renders the usage trigger. The panel fetches `/api/dsh-scope/days` same-or

igin and derives every view from that single payload.
- `conversation.session.header.actions` (order
30, after the job list) renders the lens trigger. Its popover reads three official projections — `t
okenUsage` (four buckets accumulated over the whole durable log), `contextPressure` (input-side wind
ow pressure plus the route's context window), and `contextBreakdown` (heuristic system/tools/message
composition of the next request).

## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`npm run build` emits two artifacts:
- `lib/index.js` — the Node host half. `@deepseek-ai/*` stays external and resolves against the prof

ile's own installation at runtime.
- `lib/client.js` — the browser half, wrapped in the harness Modu
leLoader factory format. Platform modules (`react`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*`) stay external and r
esolve through the loader's injected `require`; everything else, including Recharts, is inlined.
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility
Built and verified against `dsh` `0.1.0-rc.6` and `0.2.0-rc.2` (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` / `dsh-web-a
pp` bundles). The harness is in developer preview and iterates quickly — expect compatibility-breaki
). The harness is in developer preview and iterates quickly — expect compatibility-breaking changes.
The host half reads persisted logs through whichever API the installed `sessionPersistence` exposes:
`open(id, 'read')` plus `handle.read(offset)` on `0.2.x`, and the older `readFrom(id, fromSeq)` els
ewhere. `list()` is normalized to `{ header, revision }` snapshots, so both shapes fold identically.
dsh imports each plugin module once at startup, so a profile config reload cannot replace host-half
code: **restart dsh after rebuilding**.
